function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning: The user wants to start Docker on Windows using docker start. They likely want to run a command to start Docker service. On Windows, Docker Desktop runs as a service. To start Docker, you can use "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service com.docker.service". But they said "docker start". That command is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. So maybe they want to start Docker Desktop. We can instruct them to run "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service com.docker.service". Or we can use "docker start" to start a container. But the question: "start Docker on window using docker start." Might be ambiguous. Let's interpret: They want to start Docker Desktop service. So we can run "net start com.docker.service". We'll use the function to execute command.
